summary.intent: Wrap up the 0.20.1 fix PRs (#537-#540) and release PR #533, then design a language-agnostic, goal-oriented code review prompt (for Entire's review agent) and launch an agentic whole-codebase defect hunt.
summary.outcome: PRs #537-#540 were merged with #540's CI green on all 17 checks, and the worktree and local branches were cleaned up. Release PR #533 (0.20.1, seven fixes) is mergeable but waits on CI and Entire Gates approval. A lean tagged review prompt was drafted, and two agents were launched, one on plan-to-publish and one on manifests and cascade. They are running with permission to execute the binary and to report only reproduced defects.

repo: CI used `channel = "stable"` for Rust, so a new toolchain (1.100) broke clippy, test-build and coverage on #538 and #539 until #540 landed; pinning a tested version would prevent this.
Release PR #533 bundles all seven changes (#531, #534-#539); #540 is test-only and has no changeset.
Entire Gates showed `fail` on #533 and CI there needs manual approval; it is unknown whether the gate result is stale.
Merging main into branches (not rebasing) keeps signed commits intact.

Real bugs found in earlier hunts were mostly cross-module: subdirectory path handling differing across `version`, `release_decision` and `release`; fixed groups interacting with pre mode; changelog reading cascade state altered by a later group pass.
Settled decisions agents must not flag: emoji in release PR body, E194, exit-code judgment calls, Entire auto-push.
Docs consulted for invariants: ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/architecture/, docs/specs/*.json, docs/stability.md, AGENTS.md; there is no REVIEW.md.
An existing test asserted the pre-mode downgrade bug, so a passing test is not evidence of intent.
The codebase is about 46k lines across callisto-graph, callisto-cli, callisto-manifests and callisto-model crates.
workflow: Agent findings labelled 'confirmed' often lack proof; reproduce each finding with the real binary or a failing test before fixing.
Agent-based review works better when given a goal, invariants and permission to execute than when split into crate shards with handoff notes, which recreates human org-chart process.
Review prompts work better stating goal, why each rule exists, proof bar and output contract than a step-by-step method; use tags, calm tone, a stopping condition and put the Change last.
Don't make reviewers conservative in several places at once (proof, confidence floor, exclusions, author-would-fix); keep proof as the one gate.
Compare review models and prompts against an answer key of past Changes (#538, #539, #535, #528, #531 plus clean ones) scoring defects found, false positives and cost.
Scripts were often a workaround for the worktree guard rather than a real need; prefer direct commands.
Keep one PR per topic, signed commits and the repo's own checks; drop ceremony such as long PR bodies for one-line fixes.

friction: Worktree guard forced helper scripts for simple removals.
Earlier plans over-engineered with shards, boundary notes and multi-wave agents, and had to be rethought after user pushback.
Review prompt went through several rounds of simplification as it was too prescriptive.
Uncertainty about the review model ('gpt sol medium') and whether the sandbox permits running the program.
Entire Gates status on #533 is unclear and needs manual CI approval.
open_items: User must approve CI and merge release PR #533 to publish 0.20.1 after checking the Entire Gates result.
Reproduce, fix and PR separately each defect the two running agents report.
Decide OIDC trusted publishing (generated workflow vs config key, `id-token: write` on `execute`; plan in docs/projects/OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md).
Pin the CI Rust toolchain to a tested version instead of `stable`.
Another bug hunt on npm workspace and lockfile handling and the GitHub release/tag flow.
Docs PR #495 is an old draft; check if stale and close or refresh.
Build an answer key to compare review models and effort levels, and test the revised prompt on known past Changes.
Decide whether the review environment can allow running the program, and whether the UI uses the confidence field.
